sections.h2: Where is the Bedford County Register of Deeds in Shelbyville?
sections.html:
The office is at 100 West Side Square, Suite 303, Shelbyville, TN 37160. The phone number is (931) 684-5719 and the fax line is (931) 685-2086, both from the county's contact page.

The county's register of deeds page describes the office as the keeper of records that give public notice of property ownership, liens and contracts. It also says the office earns revenue from recording and filing fees and from a commission on the state conveyance and mortgage taxes it collects, and that it reports the taxes it collects to the state each month.

Two services on that page help sellers. One is an online fee calculator for anyone planning to record documents. The other is a free fraud alert sign-up that notifies a person of property transfers recorded under their name, and an owner can enroll several versions of a name, such as a nickname or a suffix. Anyone who owns a house they rarely visit, such as an inherited property, may find the alert worth setting up.

sections.h2: What should a home seller know about Bedford County?
sections.html:
Bedford County lies in the southern part of Middle Tennessee. It was created in 1807 from Rutherford County and was once the state's largest county by area, though Coffee, Moore, Lincoln and Marshall counties were later carved from it. Today it covers 475 square miles, with Shelbyville as the county seat and only city, and with Bell Buckle, Normandy and Wartrace as towns. Interstate 24, U.S. 231, U.S. 41A and a string of state routes cross it, and the county is part of the Nashville-Davidson-Murfreesboro combined statistical area.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts give a current picture:

  • 55,273 residents in July 2025, a 10.0% rise from the April 2020 base
  • 21,876 housing units, 71.9% of them owner-occupied
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes of $281,200 for 2020 to 2024
  • Median gross rent of $1,051 and median household income of $67,225
  • 378 building permits in 2025
  • Transportation and warehousing receipts of about $1.24 billion in 2022

sections.h2: How is the Tennessee transfer tax figured on a Bedford County deed?
sections.html:
Tennessee's realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100, and the buyer pays it to the register when the deed is recorded. The tax base depends on the kind of deed. A quick comparison from the Department of Revenue's recordation tax manual:

Deed typeTax base
Warranty deed or other freehold transferThe greater of the consideration or the property's value at transfer
Quitclaim deedThe consideration given, unless the wording shows an intent to convey the property itself
Warranty deed with a retained life estateFair market value minus the value of the life estate
Modified or amended deedNeeds the book and page of the earlier deed so the register can see the original tax was paid

Language such as "to have and to hold" or "in fee simple" can push a quitclaim deed onto the fair market value basis. The manual's life estate example involves a 70-year-old father who transfers a $250,000 property and keeps a life estate. The deed preparer works out the life estate value, subtracts it, and the tax base falls to $146,765, which yields $543.03 at the 2018 factors used in that example.

At the county's median home value of $281,200, the tax on an ordinary sale would be about $1,040.44. A real sale is taxed on its actual price or value.

sections.h2: What does the oath of value mean for a Bedford County sale?
sections.html:
The buyer, the buyer's agent or a trustee acting for the buyer states under oath, on the face of the deed and in the register's presence, the actual consideration or the value of the property, whichever is greater. The oath is not required when the transfer is exempt. A false statement made knowingly is punishable as perjury.

The Department of Revenue accepts the tax base shown at the local assessor's office as fair market value, or a recent appraisal that the assessor's office has accepted. Anything below that is open to audit, with penalties and interest. The department also reviews recorded deeds from counties it picks at random and compares the value claimed under oath with the assessor value on the Comptroller's website, then may send an inquiry letter to the owner on the deed.

Two rules help avoid double payment. A person who gets several deeds for the same transfer of one parcel pays the tax once, and no tax is due until title actually passes by deed.

The manual lists transfers that owe no realty transfer tax. Among them:

  • A deed by an executor carrying out a will
  • A domestic settlement decree or deed between divorcing parties
  • A release of a life estate to the remainder beneficiaries
  • A transfer to or from a revocable living trust by the same transferor or that person's spouse

sections.h2: What changes when the buyer takes out a mortgage in Bedford County?
sections.html:
A deed of trust adds a separate mortgage tax of $0.115 per $100 of indebtedness, with the first $2,000 exempt. The borrower pays it, and the register cannot record the instrument until it is paid. Every recorded instrument showing a debt must state "Maximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes is $___."

An assumption agreement matters if a buyer takes over a seller's loan. If the seller stays liable on the old debt, the manual says no new indebtedness tax is due. If the buyer signs a new contract with the lender and the seller's obligation is cancelled, tax is due on the new mortgage. A holder who does not pay the indebtedness tax owes a penalty of $250 or double the unpaid tax, whichever is greater.

Liens filed by contractors, subcontractors, laborers and mechanics, and judgment liens, are not subject to the mortgage tax. That does not remove them from the title, so a seller should ask the title company to search for them.

sections.h2: Which Bedford County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The Property Assessor is on the third floor of the courthouse annex at 100 West Side Square, Suite 301, phone (931) 684-6390. The office values all real and business personal property, keeps the tax maps and prepares the tax rolls for the trustee and municipalities. An owner who thinks the value is wrong appeals to the local board of equalization first and then to the State Board of Equalization.

The Trustee is on the first floor of the annex at 100 Public Square West, Suite 102, phone (931) 684-4303, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. In January and February the office also opens Saturdays from 8 a.m. to noon for tax payments. The trustee takes online payments through a link on the county page and administers the Tax Relief Program, which has existed since 1976 and serves homeowners 65 or older, disabled homeowners and permanently disabled veterans.

Statewide dates apply to Bedford County. Property is assessed as of January 1, current taxes are due the first Monday in October, and the prior year's taxes go delinquent on March 1. A seller with a pending sale should confirm the tax status with the trustee before closing. Tax year 2026 bills have been payable since the first Monday in October, and under the state schedule the last day to pay without interest falls at the end of February.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Bedford County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: It is at 100 West Side Square, Suite 303, Shelbyville, TN 37160. The phone number is (931) 684-5719. The county page also links an online fee calculator for people planning to record documents.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Bedford County home sale?
faqs.a: It is $0.37 per $100 of the greater of the price or the property's value, paid by the buyer. A home valued at $281,200, the county's median for owner-occupied housing, would carry about $1,040.44 of tax. Quitclaim deeds are taxed on the consideration unless the wording conveys the property itself.

faqs.q: Is any Bedford County transfer exempt from the realty transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The Department of Revenue lists several, including a deed by an executor carrying out a will, divorce settlement deeds and transfers into or out of a revocable living trust by the same person or spouse. No oath of value is needed on an exempt transfer.

faqs.q: Can I get an alert if someone records a deed in my name?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's register of deeds page offers a free fraud alert sign-up. It notifies the owner of property transfers recorded under a name, and a person can sign up with several variations of that name.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Bedford County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Trustee at 100 Public Square West, Suite 102, in Shelbyville, or use the online link on the trustee's page. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., plus Saturday mornings in January and February. Call (931) 684-4303 with questions.
